newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's LKAB 8-mo profit falls to 509 mln skr.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's LKAB 8-mo profit falls to 509 mln skr.

text.p: Swedish state-owned mining group LKAB reported on Monday a slight fall in profits for the first eight months of the year, saying the outlook for the industry remained gloomy.
LKAB's profits after tax for the period fell to 509 million crowns, down from 543 million.
"Although there are indications that the steel industry cycle will turn upwards, we have seen no real signs of this so far," LKAB said in its results statement.
Turnover rose eight percent to 3.25 billion crowns, but operating profit fell to 382 million crowns from 430 million as restructuring costs escalated.
LKAB said the full-year result would be below 1995 levels due to falling demand and the ongoing labour conflict in the Norwegian port of Narvik, where the iron ore is loaded onto ships.
In 1995 the company posted a net profit of 657 million crowns after tax.
